title: The wall clock does not bound a pi worker: the interrupt is not a stop
description:
Observed live in the Phase 3 run (epic-9pd, tick cwa, attempt 7), 2026-09-15.

The wall clock fired and stopAtWall (internal/exec/herdr/wall.go) sent interruptChord through herdr's AgentSendKeys, wrote wall_clock_exceeded, and observed 'stopped the agent … the interrupt was delivered'. It then re-delivered the same interrupt at every poll for 26+ minutes. The agent kept working. It was inside a single foreground 'make test-short' tool call that had run 28 minutes, and pi does not abort a running tool on the interrupt key.

inspect.go only settles a stopped attempt when herdr answers the agent is GONE. An interactive agent does not exit when interrupted — at best it cancels the turn and returns to its prompt; here it did not even do that. So:
- the bound does not bound spending: the agent ran and spent past it;
- the attempt is held as running indefinitely, so the run makes no progress (a stall by the measure that matters);
- the feed says nothing — the last line was 'dispatched' 85 minutes earlier. Every stop observation went to the attempt's observations.jsonl, which no watcher reads.

An earlier attempt the same day (55i) passed through the same stop without harm only because it had already written its report, so settlement came from the evidence, not from the stop.

Wanted:
1. A stop that actually stops. After the interrupt, allow a short grace period, then close the agent's pane or terminate its process tree through herdr, and settle on that positive answer. The interrupt is a courtesy, not the mechanism.
2. The wall clock firing is a FEED event (and in ticfac status), not only an observation line.
3. Interaction with pbb: a worker stopped mid-work loses uncommitted changes; the snapshot pbb asks for must happen before the pane is closed.

Acceptance should use a worker that ignores the interrupt, since that is the case that failed.
notes:
2026-09-15 17:44 - HOW IT ENDED, and three further defects from the same incident.

The reconciler's own backstop fired (dispatch.go waitForSettlement: the wall clock plus one wipe threshold of grace) at 14:50:18 and refused the attempt RefusedUnaddressed, ending the run as failed. That bounded the stall at about 85 minutes instead of forever. The backstop is right. What it left is not:

1. THE REFUSAL'S REASON REACHED NO OPERATOR SURFACE. The feed goes straight from 'dispatched cwa' at 13:24:45 to a generic run_finished ('cwa did not pass: the run stopped rather than integrating over an unproven change…'). The checkpoint reason is the same generic text. The specific refusal — unaddressed, past the wall clock, release with ticfac settle — appeared nowhere a watcher reads. It had to be recovered by reading dispatch.go. A refusal that decides a run's fate must be a feed line with its own text.

2. THE REFUSAL'S WORDING IS FOR THE WRONG FAILURE. It says 'its supervisor never settled it, and a pid that outlives its job is a number the host reuses. Nobody can say whether it is running.' That text was written for the local subprocess executor's dead supervisor. Here herdr could say exactly: the agent was alive, working, and ignoring the interrupt. The refusal should name what the executor actually observed.

3. THE WORKER WAS ORPHANED. The run ended; the agent tick-cwa-a7 was still working and spending, in a workspace nothing will clean up. Refusing an attempt as unaddressed must not leave a live agent behind — the stop in this tick must run before the refusal, not after the run is gone.

Resuming the run does not recover by itself: the settlement deadline is derived from the durable dispatch marker, so a resumed run re-reads the same live agent past the same deadline and refuses again, and ticfac settle refuses to release an attempt the executor can still address. A person has to stop the agent first.
acceptance_criteria: An agent that ignores the interrupt is terminated within a bounded grace period after its wall clock and the attempt settles; the wall clock firing writes a feed line; a test with a fake agent that ignores the interrupt key asserts both
